name: San Antonio Huitepec Mixtec
confidence_why: No description of stress in San Antonio Huitepec Mixtec has been found: the only statement is Josserand's (1983) generalization that the Mixtec couplet carries stress on its first syllable, known here only as quoted by Carroll (2015) and Penner (2019), and the Huitepec-specific works read (Julián Caballero 2009, Bradley and Josserand 1982, INALI 2006) say nothing about stress.

new_statements.quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. [...] In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec.
new_statements.citation: Carroll, Lucien Serapio. 2015. Ixpantepec Nieves Mixtec Word Prosody. PhD dissertation, University of California, San Diego, p. 86 -- quoting Josserand, J. Kathryn. 1983. Mixtec Dialect History. PhD dissertation, Tulane University, p. 180.
new_statements.locator: Carroll 2015, sec. 4.2.1, p. 86 (extracted text); Huitepec listed in Table A.2, p. 276; original statement Josserand 1983: 180
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: (extracted text of Carroll 2015 UCSD diss.) lines 5440-5443, page 86 running header: "Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior." and lines 5489-5490 (p. 87): "In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec." Both halves of the reported quote are present verbatim; the '[..]' elides Carroll's variety-by-variety survey (Nuxaa, Ayutla, Jicaltepec, Acatlan, Diuxi, Mixtepec, Atatlahuca, Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala) -- none of which is Huitepec. Table A.2 (lines 168…
new_statements.rule_in_words: second-hand AND FAMILY-WIDE ONLY: Josserand's dialect survey (which includes a San Antonio Huitepec wordlist, code 'Huit') states that the Mixtec root template, the disyllabic/bimoraic couplet, is stressed on its first syllable, i.e. stress falls on the initial syllable of the root couplet (= penultimate syllable of an unaffixed disyllabic word), with prefixes and enclitics outside the stress domain. No source seen makes this claim specifically for Huitepec Mixtec or gives Huitepec evidence.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Huitepec. Carroll notes for other varieties (Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala) that vocalic enclitics can shift stress, and (Atatlahuca) penultimate stress in polysyllables; these are not about Huitepec.
new_statements.domain_note: The statement concerns the couplet (root/stem template) across the Mixtec family, not the phonological word of Huitepec Mixtec specifically; it is Carroll's report of Josserand 1983:180, whose own text was not accessible. Huitepec Mixtec is tonal (Josserand's list is tone-marked per MixteCoDB coding notes; Julián Caballero 2009:266 mentions tense distinctions by 'un leve cambio de tono').
new_statements.identity_note: Target = mixteco de San Antonio Huitepec (municipio San Antonio Huitepec, ex-distrito Zaachila, Oaxaca; Ethnologue 'Zaachila Mixtec'), Josserand code 'Huit', MixteCoDB Group 4 / Eastern Alta-Teozacoalco, glottocode huit1252. The only stress statement located is Josserand's (1983:180) pan-Mixtec generalization as reported by Carroll 2015 (a dissertation on Ixpantepec Nieves Mixtec, Glottolog Silacayoapan [mks]); it is not a description of Huitepec Mixtec itself. Not to be confused with Cerro Huitepec (Chiapas, Tzotzil area) or Santa María Huitepec (Mixe), which dominate search results.
